findings.finding: Self-controlled practice environments improve motor learning by fostering feelings of autonomy and competence in the learner.
findings.quote: This review suggests that a self-controlled practice context can facilitate such factors as feelings of autonomy and competence of the learner, thereby supporting the psychological needs of the learner

findings.finding: Providing learners with choices, even those unrelated to the specific task, can lead to superior motor learning outcomes.
findings.quote: We hypothesized that motor learning could be enhanced by providing learners with choices - even if those choices are unrelated to task performance.

findings.finding: Self-controlled learning is a key principle for optimizing rehabilitation and improving functional performance.
findings.quote: The following key concepts to enhance rehabilitation and prepare the patient for re-integration to sports after an ACL injury that is as safe as possible are presented: (1) external focus of attention, (2) implicit learning, (3) differential learning, (4) self-controlled learning and contextual interference.

principle: Allowing learners to exercise autonomy and make choices during practice enhances motor learning by supporting their psychological needs for competence and control.
for_the_teacher: Allow the learner to choose the order of practice segments or the music track for their session.
Offer the learner the option to decide when they want to receive feedback or view a demonstration.
Provide opportunities for the learner to select minor, non-task-related preferences to increase their sense of autonomy.
